In the 100 metres 1st string our sprinter from British Guiana, Ivan Mayers, showed a clean pair of heels to his rivals to record 11.2 secs. In the 2nd string race Ron Morrell finished third, with P.
Butler, Ivan Mayers and Bob Wolton won the 1 mile medley relay, beating Mitcham, with Hercules third. Final points were:—Junior: Hercules A.C., 47; Belgrave H., 37; Mitcham A.C., 22.
In the Senior events we saw Ron Holtum win the first 100 yards, with Ivan Mayers winning the second race, and Mayers also won his 220 yards race, with Dicky Bartlett winning the other 220 yards.

Ivan Mayers won the 100 yds., with Dicky Bartlett winning the 220, and Ian Badiali was 1st in the 880, with Ray Tooby in 3rd place. Bob Taylor was 2nd in the 1 mile, with John Burr 3rd, and George Stace ran well to win the 2 miles run in 9 mins. 58 secs.

Our team was Ron Holtum, Denis Merrett, Dicky Bartlett and Ivan Mayers, and although the latter was troubled by a foot injury, the whole team ran extremely well to beat Thames Valley H., with Cambridge H. third.
We had three runners pass on to the 2nd round of the 220 yds. in Denis Merrett, Ivan Mayers and Basil Walden, but only Merrett progressed further and he was eventually 4th in the final of this event.
In the senior 4 x 110 yds., our team of Basil Walden, Ron Holtum, Denis Merrett and Ivan Mayers won their heat in 44.1 secs., the same time as the Polytechnic H., who were the eventual winners.
Our members did well at the Charlotteville " open " meeting on Whit-Monday, and Ivan Mayers and Ian Forrester were 1st and 2nd in both the 100 and 220 yds. handicaps.

Ron handed over to Basil Walden who put in a terrific challenge to hand over to Ivan Mayers about 1½ yards up. T.V.H. had Downs on the last leg and I thought he might rob us of our first win in this event but with 50 yards to go I saw Ivan's face break into a grin and I knew that it was ours.
In the Shot Put Ted Gaworski gave us his usual Boxing Day exhibition of class putting. A stanger in this event was Ivan Mayers who made the most of his 3yd. 1ft.6in.

Ivan Mayers reached the semi-final of the 220 yards in which he ran extremely well and Ted Gaworski gave his usual polished performances in the Shot and Discus, although not reaching the coveted placed positions.

Ivan Mayers was 2nd and Dennis Merrett 3rd in the 100 yards and Ivan also 2nd in the 220. B.H.Morris ran a fine race in the 440 yards to finish third to two internationals and Pete Bagnall filled the same place in the steeple chase.

We also had a victory in the 100 yards in which Ivan Mayers and Denis Merrett finished 1st and 2nd. We missed Ray Tooby - who failed to make an appearance - in the 880 yards, but George Davidson carried our colours and came 5th.

On May 2nd a few of our athletes were engaged at the Leyton Flood Light meeting and it was pleasing to have Ivan Mayers running so well over the 100 yards in really first class company to finish 4th in 10.1secs.

Of the events, five were on the field and the contribution of our boys in this section was 27 points to our grand total. Outstanding recollections of the meeting were a fine sprint double by Ivan Mayers, some grand half miling by J.
Ivan Mayers was also in the team and was placed 3rd in the 100 yards and was a member of the winning Relay team. At the Universities Athletic Championships held at Manchester on 26th May, J.P.
Most notable were the brilliant doubles of Brian Morris (Sussex 220 & 440 yds.), Ivan Mayers (Middlesex 100 & 220 yds.) and Clive Ryan (Surrey Junior 100 & 220 yds.).
The Field Events Section however, were conspicuous by their absence, as will be seen by the fact that Ivan Mayers won the Shot Put in addition to completing the double in the sprints.
Ivan Mayers equalled his own 9.9s. 100 yards record at the Kinnaird meeting. I should be interested to learn Mal Ash's heat time in the Kinnaird, or in the final if his time was taken.

In the Hop Step & Jump, a keen battle ensued between Norman Caves, Charlie Jones and Ivan Mayers. Norman eventually won with a 44'9" effort, but one wonders just how far Ivan would have got had he not repeatedly taken off well before the board - a very interesting contest to watch.
The shot brought out former sprinter Ivan Mayers, still talking of another short season, who was second; the winner being Dave Butler.
The teams of 1954, which included such athletes as Ivan Mayers and Clay Gibbs, have long since retired - excepting Ron of course, who is still most active.
Maurice O'Dell - 100 yds Championship 1925 - 1931 inclusive. 6. 1954 - team: Dennis Merrett,Ron Holtum,Basil Waldon,Ivan Mayers.

Belgrave's only win in the A.A.A. senior sprint relay championship came in 1954 when on July 31st at Birmingham the team of Dennis Merrett, Ron Holtum, Basil Walden and Ivan Mayers won their 4 x 110yds heat in 42.9 and then went on to take the final with the second best time recorded by a club team - 42.6.
Ivan Mayers
The West Indies gave us a great sprinter in Ivan Mayers who anchored our winning team in the A.A.A. 4 x 100 metres Relay Team in 1954, he too represented his country.

Denis Merrett sprang a surprise with an excellent double in both sprints, defeating Basil Walden and Ivan Mayers. The 440 went as expected to Alan Sexton in the good time of 50.6 in atrocious conditions with Jim Heathfield 2nd.
Bob Taylor equalled the Middlesex record held by the great Arthur Wint in the 880 yards, and Ivan Mayers beat Ron Holtum in the sprints while Jack Brown won the Kent one mile.
